To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the network of no-take and partially-protected marine reserves within the Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park has resulted in increased fish abundances and richness; 2) there was a strong relationship between compliance and reserve performance, but not between reserve size and reserve performance; and 3) partially-protected areas did not have additional conservation benefits compared to fully protected areas.

(1) fish assemblages in a network of newly established no-take marine protected areas had greater abundances and diversity compared to two different types of protected areas with partial restrictions on fishing, (2) the benefits of protection were greatest in the no-take areas that received the most compliance actions, and (3) the two different types of partial protection areas did not differ from one another.

(1) the establishment of a network of marine protected areas can lead to increases in the abundance and richness of fish assemblages; (2) the effectiveness of individual marine reserves is related to their management, and not their size; and (3) partially-protected areas provide little additional conservation benefits for fish assemblages, and may not be a suitable conservation tool in this region.
